correctness.summary: Every total dominating set of C(G) decomposes into a vertex cover A of G and subdivision vertices corresponding to an edge set covering exactly the residual vertices R_G(A). The converse construction is exact. The residual partial edge-cover number equals |R|-nu(G[R]). All 995 connected Graph-Atlas graphs of orders 2 through 7 independently agree with direct total-domination MILPs.

limitations: The optimization identity is not claimed to yield a polynomial-time algorithm.
The 2020 central-tree article was inspected through its abstract and bibliographic record rather than its complete theorem text.
An equivalent result under differently indexed terminology remains a residual originality risk.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The closest directly inspected 2019 source gives only the general bounds tau(G) <= gamma_t(C(G)) <= tau(G)+rho(G) and family-specific formulas. Searches over total domination, central graphs, vertex covers, edge covers, complement formulations and matching formulations did not locate the exact optimization identity or the complement equality criterion. The 2020 central-tree paper remains the principal partially inspected source.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The theorem converts the foundational general bounds for total domination of central graphs into an exact structural formula for every graph without isolated vertices, identifies the residual cost through the matching number of an induced residual subgraph, and characterizes equality with the vertex-cover lower bound.
